title: Senior Sales Manager - Media (m/w/d)
Frontend Engineer - Agentic AI
description:
About Us 

Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 

Your Mission

As a Frontend Engineer at Hawk, you will build and maintain the user interface of our agentic AI Investigation Agent. This is the product where compliance analysts configure AI workflows, watch autonomous investigations run, and review, question and act on what the agent concludes.

The frontend is a modern TypeScript monorepo made of a host application and a growing set of independently deployable microfrontends. These remotes are designed to be built once and used in two places: our new shadcn/ui-based Investigation Agent and our existing Material UI-based Case Manager. Your job is to understand this codebase deeply, keep it healthy, and ship new features with care, from the component level all the way to how it is built and deployed.

What You'll Work On:

  • Features: Build product features end to end in React and TypeScript, such as workflow graph editors, investigation timelines, data-heavy tables and dashboards that make agentic AI output understandable for analysts.

  • Microfrontends: Develop and maintain Module Federation remotes, keep remote/host contracts stable, and make sure features fit into both the Investigation Agent and the MUI-based Case Manager.

  • Design system and data layer: Contribute to our shared shadcn/ui + Tailwind component library (documented in Storybook), and consume our Python/FastAPI backends through OpenAPI-generated clients with TanStack Query and Router.

  • Build, test and deploy: Work in a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo with GitHub Actions CI, Vitest and Playwright tests, and deployments to AWS including per-PR preview environments.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with Product, UX, backend engineers and Data Science, and use AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor as part of your everyday workflow.

Your Profile:

  • 3–5 years building and maintaining production React applications, with strong TypeScript and modern React skills (hooks, composition, performance, complex state and forms).

  • Clean frontend architecture: you structure code around features and clear boundaries. You keep UI components presentational and reusable, put data fetching and business logic in hooks and typed API layers, and keep server state separate from local UI state. You prefer composition, small focused components and strict typing, and you treat cross-module contracts as an API.

  • Design-system experience: hands-on work with a component-library approach, ideally shadcn/ui, Radix and Tailwind. Familiarity with Material UI is a strong plus.

  • Microfrontends and delivery: Module Federation or similar runtime composition, shared dependencies and host/remote contracts, plus the build and deployment basics behind them: Vite, monorepos (pnpm workspaces, Turborepo or Nx), CI pipelines (GitHub Actions)

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you're happy working on problems that aren't fully defined yet. You ask the right questions, make sensible assumptions, build a first version and refine it with Product and UX, without waiting for a perfect spec.

  • AI tooling: daily, practical use of AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.).

  • Communication: clear communication in English, and the ability to explain technical decisions to both technical and non-technical colleagues.

Bonus:

  • Some Python: enough to read a FastAPI endpoint or Pydantic model, run the backend locally, trace a bug across the API boundary, or open a small backend PR. You don't need to be a backend engineer.

  • Infrastructure as code: exposure to Terraform or AWS CDK.

  • Quality tooling: Storybook-driven development, visual regression testing or accessibility testing.

  • Auth: Auth0/OIDC integration in single-page apps.

  • Domain interest: UX for AI products, or previous work in fintech, RegTech or compliance.

title: Senior Quality Assurance Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
ZEAL Network SE is a leading international provider of online lottery products, operating for over 20 years with brands like LOTTO24 and Tipp24. As Germany’s largest digital lottery operator and a trusted partner of Spain’s ONCE, we are passionate about shaping the future of lottery experiences.

 

Freiheit+ is one of ZEAL's new German state-licensed social lottery that gives participants the chance to win €5,000 every month for 15 years, plus a one-time prize of €250,000. Every ticket sold supports educational projects, with at least 30% of proceeds directly funding initiatives for a good cause. Freiheit+ perfectly combines the dream of lifelong financial freedom with the opportunity to make a real difference, reflecting ZEAL’s commitment to offering innovative, socially impactful lottery experiences.

As a Senior Quality Assurance Engineer (f/m/d), you'll be the guardian of product quality, ensuring our solutions meet the highest standards throughout the entire development lifecycle.

Your tasks:

  • Own, expand and nurture our E2E test pipeline, keeping it stable, fast and reliable, and enabling tests for other teams while offering our own tests for integration into their pipelines.

  • Continuously improve our tests using new technologies and approaches.

  • Build a solid functional and high-level technical understanding of company-wide processes to effectively test complex user flows and identify edge cases.

What you offer us:

  • Several years of experience and a strong background in testing web applications.

  • Extensive hands-on experience in creating and maintaining automated frontend tests.

  • Thinking outside the box and exploring multiple ways to test, including E2E UI tests, accessibility, page performance, and more.

  • Active communication and collaboration with other QAs to share knowledge, exchange best practices, and learn from each other.

  • Proficiency in the Playwright test framework using TypeScript, or comparable hands-on experience with other modern E2E frameworks such as Cypress.

  • Experience in maintaining and improving CI/CD test pipelines, including diagnosing and resolving flaky tests.

  • A solid grasp of working within a microservices environment where features are frequently and rapidly released (continuous delivery).

  • An enthusiasm for collaborative work within self-organized teams, coupled with the willingness to take full ownership and responsibility for quality topics.

  • A proactive communication style and excellent communication skills in English, fostering a collaborative and cooperative atmosphere; German is appreciated but not required.

What we offer:

title: Project Delivery Lead (m/f/d)
description:
Build something monumental for Healthcare!

At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care.

We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you!

We are looking for a Project Delivery Lead to join our Implementation team in the DACH region (Germany, Austria and Switzerland). You will own the successful deployment of Tandem in large organisations, from planning through go-live and adoption.
This is a hands-on role with real autonomy. You will coordinate clinicians, hospital leadership, IT teams and colleagues across Tandem to make complex deployments happen. You will own the outcome, while having significant freedom in how you get there.
Because we are scaling quickly, you will also help shape how we implement Tandem. We don't have every process figured out yet, and we want someone who enjoys creating structure, solving problems and making things work better.

Who you are

  • You are motivated by improving clinical workflows and reducing clinician admin burden.

  • You are structured, proactive and highly accountable. When given a complex objective, you create the plan, figure out what needs to happen and make sure it happens.

  • You are operationally strong and capable of running implementation plans end-to-end, including stakeholder alignment and structured project management.

  • You work well in a fast-changing environment and know when a situation calls for judgement rather than a standard approach. You enjoy taking ownership and turning complexity into action.

  • You are analytical enough to break down complex problems, but practical enough to get into the details. You don't just flag problems. You work out what needs to happen next and drive it forward.

  • You likely have 3+ years of experience in a demanding environment such as management consulting, technology, healthcare operations, a start-up or scale-up, or project/programme management.



You bring:

  • Strong project management and organisational skills, with a track record of delivering complex projects on time and to scope

  • Proven experience delivering projects in hospitals, ideally multi-site rollouts across large hospital groups

  • Experience setting up and running project governance, such as steering committees, workstreams and regular status reporting

  • Experience leading cross-functional project teams and driving results without direct authority

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication, from clinical staff on the ward to senior leadership

  • Experience in change management and driving adoption in clinical environments

  • Proven experience with the German-speaking hospital landscape, including hospital IT systems, data protection and compliance approvals, and works or staff council processes

  • A strong bias towards action and ownership

  • The ability to work independently and structure ambiguous problems

  • Professional fluency in German and English (C1 or higher)



What you will do

  • Own large, mainly hospital, deployments end-to-end, including project plans, timelines, dependencies, risks and stakeholder alignment

  • Coordinate clinicians, hospital leadership, IT, data protection and information security officers, and internal teams to keep deployments moving

  • Prepare and support teams through training and go-live, including regular on-site work across Germany, Austria and Switzerland

  • Drive adoption after go-live and work with clinical champions to identify and address barriers

  • Proactively identify and resolve issues, bringing the right people together when you need support

  • Work closely with internal specialists such as MedOps and TechOps, who own parts of the implementation that fit their expertise, while you drive the project and remain accountable for the overall outcome

  • Improve our implementation approach by developing better processes, tools and ways of working as we scale



What you will get

  • Real ownership and autonomy from day one

  • The opportunity to directly shape how AI is adopted in healthcare

  • The chance to grow your career while making a meaningful impact on the future of healthcare within a fast-growing European healthtech scale-up

  • Exposure to clinicians, hospital leadership, technology and commercial teams

  • Competitive salary and quarterly bonus

  • Regular team events and an international, high-performing team



Location
We believe the best ideas happen when we're together. This is a full-time role based in Munich, Germany.
This role involves regular travel across the DACH region and may include extended on-site periods during go-lives.

Culture at Tandem

At Tandem, we move fast, think big, and take ownership. We're a high-performing, diverse team with a shared drive to change the future of healthcare - and we’re just getting started.

Our culture is built on action, ambition, and learning. You'll be trusted to take the lead, challenge yourself, and make an impact from day one. We believe real growth happens when you're stretched, supported, and surrounded by smart, passionate teammates who want to win together.

Even though we’re spread across countries, we come together often in Sweden for team meetings, social events, and offsites - blending global reach with real human connection.

We hire for talent, potential, and attitude - valuing different backgrounds and fresh perspectives. Great ideas come from everywhere, and we’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change.

Tandem handles sensitive patient data and will conduct a background check before hiring any candidate.

title: Engineering Manager - Data Platform (m/f/d)
description:
At Statista, we’re all about facts and data, for we are the world's leading business data platform. By providing reliable and easy-to-use data as well as various data analytics products and services, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

Your Job

As Engineering Manager, Data Platform at Statista, you’ll lead the engineers building a platform-as-a-product that helps teams manage and share trusted data. You’ll make it easier for data producers to get started while ensuring the platform is secure, reliable and cost-conscious as it grows.

You’ll work closely with the Senior Platform Product Manager: they lead product vision and priorities; you lead the people, technical delivery and day-to-day operation of the platform. The role spans Snowflake-based data infrastructure and event streaming via Kafka.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and grow the team. Lead a mixed team of DevOps, software and data engineers with shared ownership, on-call and standards. Grow people through clear expectations, regular feedback and real ownership, and hire as the platform grows.

  • Run the platform as a product. Partner with the Senior Platform Product Manager, make it easy for teams to put their data on the platform: quick setup, fast reviews, clear documentation, and a say in how the platform develops. Work with data producers, Analytics Engineering and other Statista group companies as partners, not just users.

  • Build trust into the platform. Guide the use of access controls, cost safeguards, audits, data contracts and metadata so teams can share data safely with people, APIs and AI-powered applications.

  • Own reliable event streaming. Run Kafka as the backbone that distributes data and content across Statista: reliable, well monitored, and easy for teams to publish to and consume from.

  • Set technical direction. Guide architecture and build-versus-buy decisions, review designs and pull requests, and use AI and automation where they improve the team's work. You'll stay technically engaged without being expected to code every day.

 

Your Skills

  • At least five years of experience leading engineering teams, ideally in data platforms, platform engineering or infrastructure. You know how to develop senior engineers and unite people with different technical backgrounds.

  • A strong foundation in data or platform engineering, with the confidence to contribute to architecture discussions and design reviews. You're familiar with cloud data warehouses, ideally Snowflake, and tools or practices such as dbt and orchestration.

  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code (IaC) using Terraform. You're comfortable with Kubernetes, CI/CD and AWS.

  • Experience operating event-streaming systems such as Kafka, Amazon MSK, Confluent or Redpanda, including a schema registry.

  • You understand data governance, including access models, data contracts, catalogues and lineage. You balance useful safeguards with a straightforward experience for the teams using the platform.

  • You use AI tools and agentic workflows in your daily work and help your team do the same. You understand how AI agents consume data and know how to make the platform and its data assets work well for agents accessing them through MCP or A2A.

What we offer

In addition to our great team, culture, and our shared goal of empowering people with data, there are many other things that make Statista a great place to work! Join us and benefit from:

  • Work from abroad up to 30 calendar days a year

  • Hybrid work and flex-time

  • International team and social events

  • Subsidized urban mobility and access to fitness and wellness options

  • Free access to Langdock and all its amazing functionalities

  • Career & training opportunities

  • Attractive locations and modern offices

  • Mental health support with OpenUp

title: Flow Lead (m/w/d
description:
At Knuspr, we’re redefining grocery shopping. Delivering fresh, local produce and everyday essentials to thousands of customers daily requires an ultra-efficient operational backbone.

As Flow Lead / Central Flow Lead, you will serve as the central command point for labor allocation and operational flow across our Fulfillment Centers in Germany. Operating from your desk, you will monitor real-time operational performance, dynamically allocate workforce capacity, and coordinate with on-site teams to keep every site running at peak efficiency.

Your mission is simple: turn live data into immediate action. By anticipating bottlenecks, balancing labor across sectors, and keeping operations aligned, you’ll ensure every order is processed seamlessly and delivered on time.

Why this role is exciting

  • Impact at scale: Directly influence labor allocation and operational output across Germany’s Fulfillment Centers from a single, centralized control tower.

  • Real-time decision-making: Work in a dynamic environment where live data translates directly into high-impact operational adjustments.

  • Smart logistics & tech: Drive performance at the intersection of automation, WMS platforms, and data-driven workforce management.

  • True ownership: Anticipate disruptions, resolve bottlenecks early, and maintain optimal operational flow under pressure.

What you’ll do

  • Control the flow: Monitor real-time dashboards and direct automated labor flow by assigning team members across individual sectors through central control tools.

  • Balance capacity dynamically: Adjust workforce distribution and shift plans on the fly in response to fluctuating order volumes and site priorities.

  • Drive operational KPIs: Track CPT (Critical Pull Time), SLAs, idle time, and sector efficiency—identifying bottlenecks early and executing timely interventions.

  • Keep teams aligned: Partner closely with Area Managers, Operations Managers, and on-site shop floor teams to execute adjustments and maintain consistent operational standards.

  • Optimize continuously: Analyze shift performance, identify recurring process gaps, review SOP compliance with site teams, and contribute feedback for next-generation labor management tools.

What we are looking for

  • Relevant operational background: Experience in dispatch, logistics, operational planning, supply chain, e-commerce, or fulfillment (experience with automated warehouses or labor scheduling is a plus).

  • Control-tower mindset: Strong ability to connect the dots across complex, fast-paced operations and make confident, data-driven decisions under pressure.

  • Tech confidence: Comfortable steering operations using real-time dashboards, WMS platforms, and automated labor allocation tools.

  • Strong language & communication skills: Very good English for daily operations and reporting, combined with strong Romanian language skills for direct, clear coordination with shop floor teams.

  • Shift availability: Willingness to work in a 3-shift system from Monday to Friday.

  • Structured & proactive approach: A problem-solver who anticipates disruptions rather than just reacting to them.

What we offer on top of your base salary

  • Daily meal allowance: An additional €9.00 tax-free meal allowance for every working day

  • Daily travel allowance: An additional €5.00 daily subsidy toward your commuting costs

  • Semi-annual vouchers: €300.00 in vouchers issued twice a year (€600 total annually)

  • Knuspr Xtra Account: 10% cashback on your orders returned directly as Knuspr credits

  • CorporateBenefits perks: Great discounts on fitness, travel, event tickets, shopping, and more

title: Senior HW Engineer – PCB Layout
description:
The Opportunity

Lumai's optical engine only works if the electronics around it hold up. Our boards carry large FPGAs and custom ASICs, multi-gigabit links and fine-pitch packages, and they have to be laid out to tolerances that leave no room for guesswork. This role takes the designs coming out of our hardware and SI/PI teams and turns them into manufacturable, high-layer-count boards.

The Role

You will own board layout from schematic handoff to fabrication release. That covers stackups and HDI structures, controlled-impedance routing, differential pairs, length and phase matching, BGA breakout for large fine-pitch devices, and the full manufacturing package: Gerber/ODB++, drill files, assembly drawings and fabrication notes. You will also own the footprint and symbol libraries, the design rules and the CAD standards the rest of the team works to.

What is genuinely hard about it is that the constraints are real and they conflict. Signal integrity, power integrity, thermal and mechanical requirements all land on the same square centimetres, and the fabricator's process limits decide what is actually buildable. You will be the person who turns simulation output into layout rules and who can defend a stackup to a fabricator.

By month six, you will have taken at least one board through to fabrication release, set the libraries and design rules the team works from, and be the first point of contact for our fabricators and assembly houses.

What You'll Do

  • Lay out dense, high-layer-count PCBs from schematic through to fabrication release, using constraint-driven flows.

  • Implement controlled-impedance routing, differential pair and length/phase matching, and HDI structures including microvias, via-in-pad and back-drilling.

  • Plan BGA breakout and component placement for large FPGAs, custom ASICs and fine-pitch packages, balancing SI, PI, thermal and mechanical requirements.

  • Translate SI/PI and hardware constraints into layout rules, and iterate quickly with engineers on simulation feedback.

  • Run DFM, DFA and DFT reviews, and act as the main technical contact with PCB fabricators and assembly houses.

  • Generate complete manufacturing outputs (Gerber/ODB++, drill files, assembly drawings, fabrication notes) and manage design revisions.

  • Own and maintain the footprint and symbol libraries, CAD standards and design templates, compliant with IPC standards.

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • Extensive professional experience laying out complex, high-speed, high-layer-count boards, with a portfolio of designs that went into production.

  • Expert proficiency in Cadence Allegro, including Constraint Manager. Equivalent Altium experience will also be considered.

  • Hands-on experience with HDI technologies: microvias, via-in-pad, stacked and staggered vias, and back-drilling.

  • Proven BGA breakout and placement for large, fine-pitch devices such as FPGAs and ASICs.

  • Thorough working knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-6012) and of DFM/DFA/DFT principles.

Strong preference for

  • Boards carrying 56G+ SerDes, PCIe Gen5/6 or DDR5 interfaces.

  • Working closely with SI/PI simulation engineers.

  • Rigid-flex, RF or mixed-signal layouts.

  • ECAD/MCAD collaboration on thermal and mechanical integration.

  • Experience setting up CAD standards, libraries and design templates in a growing team.

About Lumai

Lumai is the optical compute company building the next generation of AI infrastructure. Spun out of optics research at the University of Oxford in 2021, we compute with light instead of electrons. Our 3D optical technology carries out the matrix multiplications at the heart of AI inside beams of light travelling through free space, which lets it go beyond the limits of both silicon GPUs and integrated photonics.

In April 2026 we launched Iris Nova, the world's first optical computing system to run billion-parameter large language models in real time, using up to 90% less energy than conventional GPU-based systems. Iris Nova, the first server in the family, is now available for evaluation by hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises and research institutions. Aura and Tetra will follow.

Our work won the Falling Walls Award for Science Breakthrough of the Year 2025 and 'Best Overall Technology' at the OCP Future Technologies Symposium. We are headquartered in Oxford.

Why Lumai

You'll work on a new kind of computer. Optical computing for AI has been promised for decades. We have a working system running real models, and the hard part left is taking it to volume.

Your work ships. We are moving from first product to volume production, so what you build this year goes into the servers our customers run.

You'll work across disciplines. Optical engineers, machine learning researchers, and hardware and software engineers solve problems together. You will learn things that don't appear on your job description.

The work matters beyond Lumai. AI's appetite for energy is one of the defining constraints of the next decade. Our mission is sustainable intelligence at global scale: AI that is faster, cheaper to run and far less power-hungry.

You'll join early. You'll have a real say in how we build the product, the team and the way we work.

Equal Opportunity

Lumai is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. If you need an adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, let us know and we will do our best to support you.

description:
Job Title: Defence Account Director

Location: London; full in-office working as default

Start date: ASAP

Reports to: CCO

Compensation: Salary and Equity options available for discussion

Clearance: Must be eligible to hold UK Security Vetting Clearance SC or above (no prior clearance required)

Application deadline: 01/11/26 at 23:59 UK time

___________________________________________________________________________

Help make sovereign AI operational for UK Defence

Cosine is a UK AI lab building models, applications and infrastructure for mission-critical organisations.

We build coding agents, specialised Lumen models, AI-native security products and the infrastructure required to deploy advanced AI in demanding environments. We are also training Lumen Sovereign, the first frontier large language model trained in the UK, with the support of the UK Government.

Defence is a strategic priority for Cosine.

AI will change how Defence operates, from software engineering and intelligence analysis to cyber security, command and control, logistics and frontline operations. The challenge is turning advanced AI into capability that is trusted, secure, sovereign and useful in the real world.

We are looking for a Defence Account Director to help build that business.

This is not a traditional defence sales role. You will understand where Cosine can make a genuine operational difference, identify the right customers and programmes, shape credible opportunities and help turn early conversations into funded pilots, programmes and long-term customer relationships.

You will work closely with Cosine’s Defence Lead, technical teams and senior leadership. You will build relationships across the MOD, the Armed Forces, wider Government and the UK defence industry, while helping define Cosine’s position in the emerging sovereign AI market.

___________________________________________________________________________

What you’ll do

  • Build and own a prioritised Defence account and opportunity strategy.

  • Develop trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across the MOD, Front Line Commands, wider Government and defence industry.

  • Identify operational problems, programmes and capability gaps where Cosine can make a material difference.

  • Translate customer needs into clearly defined use cases, propositions, pilots and programmes.

  • Navigate Defence stakeholders, budgets, acquisition routes, procurement processes and decision-making structures.

  • Lead opportunities from initial conversation through demonstration, technical evaluation, commercial agreement and delivery.

  • Work with Cosine’s technical teams to create credible customer propositions without overpromising.

  • Develop relationships with primes, strategic partners and specialist technology companies where this creates a stronger route to market.

  • Maintain disciplined account planning, pipeline management, qualification and forecasting.

  • Bring structured customer and market insight back to Product, Engineering, ML and senior leadership.

___________________________________________________________________________

What we’re looking for

You may have served in the UK Armed Forces or worked closely with Defence in engineering, capability development, acquisition, procurement, digital transformation or technology adoption.

You may subsequently have worked in consulting, technology, industry or an advisory role. What matters is that you understand how Defence works and can turn a customer need into commercial momentum.

You should have:

  • Meaningful experience of the UK Defence ecosystem.

  • Strong existing relationships across Defence, Government or industry, and the ability to build new ones.

  • Experience introducing, acquiring or adopting complex technology.

  • The ability to structure ambiguous problems and turn them into actionable opportunities.

  • Strong commercial judgement and comfort being accountable for pipeline, opportunities and revenue.

  • The confidence to engage with operators, engineers, procurement teams, senior civil servants, military leaders and industry executives.

  • Genuine technical curiosity and the ability to learn enough about AI to have credible conversations with technical teams and customers.

  • The resilience to work through long Defence sales cycles while maintaining urgency and focus.

  • The independence and judgement to operate in a scale-up where the playbook is still being written.

You do not need to be an AI expert when you join. You do need to be intellectually curious, technically literate and able to communicate clearly without hiding behind jargon.

___________________________________________________________________________

What success looks like

Success ultimately means winning business and building enduring customer relationships. We aim to onboard at least 10 new client logos within the Defence account over the next 12 months and increase revenues by at least 300%. We expect that growth to come through credibility, judgement, customer insight and persistence rather than transactional selling.

In your first few months, you will:

  • Build a clear view of Cosine’s Defence proposition, capabilities and priorities.

  • Establish a focused account and stakeholder map.

  • Develop relationships with priority customers and partners.

  • Identify and qualify the most promising opportunities.

  • Create a disciplined approach to account planning, pipeline and forecasting.

Over time, you will help convert those opportunities into funded demonstrations, pilots and programmes, while shaping how Cosine is understood and adopted across UK Defence.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why this role matters

Defence does not need more AI demonstrations that remain disconnected from operations.

It needs technology that can work across real missions, real systems, real security constraints and real acquisition processes.

You will help make that happen.

This is an opportunity to build Cosine’s Defence business from the ground up, with direct access to leadership and technical teams and genuine influence over our product, market strategy and customer relationships.

If you understand Defence from the inside, have strong customer instincts and want to help make sovereign AI operational, this is an opportunity to have significant impact.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why join Cosine

  • Build a strategically important business from the ground up.

  • Work at the intersection of frontier AI, Defence and national capability.

  • Sell a genuinely differentiated product into mission-critical environments.

  • Influence product direction and go-to-market strategy.

  • Work closely with a small, technically deep and ambitious team.

  • Receive meaningful early equity with genuine upside.

___________________________________________________________________________

 

Compensation, Benefits & Ways of Working

We’re an in-office team, five days a week, by design. We believe the work we’re doing benefits from being together, collaborating closely, and building shared context.

 

What you can expect:

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market

  • Equity / share options, so you share in the upside you help create

  • 30 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Work hard in the office, collaborate closely, and switch off properly

  • Dog-friendly office — bring your dog to work

  • Weekly team breakfast & lunch

  • Monthly socials

  • Pension

  • High-quality equipment to do your best work

We care about focus, sustainability, and doing great work — not performative overwork. We value people who show up, contribute thoughtfully, collaborate well with their colleagues, and then go home.

This role won’t suit everyone. But if you’re looking for a fast-moving environment, close collaboration, and a team that takes both the work and work-life balance seriously, it’s a great place to be.

Agency & Data Protection Notice

This ensures appropriate privacy notices, lawful processing, auditability, and consistent retention controls.

description:

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce.

Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we become liable for a merchant's taxes. Sometimes we become the legal reseller in each market and carry the payments, tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

We go live wherever a merchant needs to sell next, for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack - payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're looking for a Payment Operations hire to own the part of Outpost where the money actually moves.

When we become the legal reseller in a market, we take the payment. Every merchant we onboard gets its own merchant ID and its own merchant category code, never pooled into one shared code, which is exactly why our approval rates beat the alternatives. Keeping that true across every market, every processor and every merchant is the job.

This is a quantitative role in an operational seat. You'll live in the transaction data: why authorisation rates differ by market, issuer, card type and hour of day, what a routing change is actually worth, where a 40 basis point cost difference is hiding, which decline codes are recoverable and which are noise. Then you'll act on it, with processors, with engineering, and with merchants.

You won't be siloed. Payments at Outpost touches pricing, treasury, tax and the product roadmap, and you'll be pulled into all of it. But your edge is the numbers, and we want someone whose first instinct on any problem is to pull the data and model it.

You'll work directly with the founding team and with engineering, who will build what you spec.

🧗 What You'll Get

Yes, the work is intense. But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access.

You'll own economics that decide whether the company is profitable, negotiate with processors and banks as a principal rather than a customer, and get to see the full machinery of cross-border payments from the inside. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard.

🧩 What You'll Do

Build the system

  • Run payment operations agentically. Build agentic system that monitor approval rates, triage declines, assemble dispute evidence, chase reconciliation breaks and draft the processor follow-up, so humans only touch the exceptions. You'll design the workflows, set the guardrails, and audit what the agents produce

  • Write the playbooks: new processor onboarding, new market launch, incident response, dispute handling

  • Onboard new processors, banking partners and local acquiring as we launch new markets

Own payments performance

  • Own approval rates by market, processor, issuer, card type and merchant, and know why each one moves

  • Build and run routing logic. Decide what goes where, prove the uplift, and iterate

  • Run decline recovery: retry logic, network tokens, account updater, 3DS strategy and exemption handling

  • Run chargeback operations and fraud strategy. Set thresholds, represent disputes, keep merchants inside scheme limits

  • Own the payment incident path. When authorisations drop in one market at, you're the one who spots it and fixes it

Own the economics

  • Build full visibility into cost per transaction: scheme fees, interchange, processor margin, FX, and where each one leaks

  • Own processor relationships day to day. Performance reviews, pricing negotiations, new partner evaluation

  • Model the trade-off between approval rate and cost by market, and make the call

  • Feed real payment economics into how we price merchants

Own the money movement

  • Settlement, reconciliation and payouts. Every penny accounted for, every break chased down

  • Reserve logic and settlement timing by merchant segment and risk profile

  • Work with treasury on funding, FX exposure and cash timing across our local companies

💥 Example Projects

  • Take a market from a 66% approval rate to 90% or better, and prove exactly which changes did it

  • Build the routing framework that optimises approval rate against cost, market by market

  • Renegotiate processor pricing using our own volume and performance data

  • Build the cost-per-transaction model across every processor and market, and find the basis points nobody is watching

  • Debug delays in settlement and fix them across engineering, operations and the processor

  • Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it

  • Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy

  • Evaluate and onboard a new processor for local acquiring in Latin America or Asia

  • Build the payments monitoring layer so anomalies find us, not the other way round

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • A STEM or quantitative degree is strongly preferred - mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, statistics, econometrics or similar.

  • 3 to 7+ years in payment operations, payment analytics, or a data or analytics role that moved into payments, at a processor, acquirer, or high-volume fintech (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, Worldpay, Revolut, Wise, Dojo, Airwallex or similar)

  • Strong analytical skills — advanced Excel or Sheets, experience with BI tools, and the ability to build models and run analyses independently without waiting for a data team.

  • Bonus: experience at platforms that act as the legal reseller (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), local acquiring outside Europe and the US, interchange and scheme fee economics, or a background in data science or quantitative consulting before payments

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action. You solve, you don't observe

  • Analytically strong and commercially sharp. You quantify the opportunity before you argue for it

  • Systems thinker who still does the work. You fix the transaction, then remove the reason it broke

  • Strong EQ. Processors, banks and merchants all need managing, often at the same time

  • Exceptionally hard working. You see work as a core part of your purpose

  • Fluent in ambiguity and chaos. Startups are not neat, this will be hard

  • Curious and resourceful. You can figure anything out

  • Clear, quantified achievements on your CV, not vague descriptions

What this role is not:

  • Not a payments strategy role without operational depth. You'll be in the dashboards daily

  • Not a pure analytics role. The analysis is the start, the change is the job

  • Not a narrow specialist seat. Payments here touches pricing, treasury, tax and product

  • Not for someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective

🚀 Why This Role Is Different

Most companies treat payments as a cost centre someone else manages. Here it is the product and the margin at the same time.

We take legal responsibility for our merchants' payments. That means a point of approval rate is real revenue for them and real evidence for us, and a basis point of cost is real profit. Very few people get to own that surface this early, with this much data and this little bureaucracy in the way.

We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way.

🦾 Outpost Team

Our team were leaders at Revolut, Airwallex, Adyen and Wayflyer, and we're backed by top-tier investors who have built or backed some of the world's leading fintechs.

  • World-class training from operators who've scaled globally

  • A global mission with real impact

  • Low politics, high output

  • Chance to grow into a senior leadership role

  • A culture of builders, not talkers

We work together in person in London 5 days a week. We believe the hardest problems are solved in the room.

The core of this role is investigative. When a query comes in from a banking partner, we need someone who can trace a transaction end-to-end through our systems, understand what the bank is actually asking, produce a response that meets their expectations, and critically, question what they find along the way rather than closing the thread at the first plausible answer.

Alongside partner queries, you’ll carry out merchant risk monitoring as part of the broader fraud and risk operation; reviewing merchant behaviour, flagging anomalies, and feeding intelligence into the fraud detection and response process led by the Fraud & Risk Manager. • Act as the primary point of contact for inbound risk and compliance queries from Ryft’s

acquiring and banking partners — managing each query through to full resolution.

reconstructing the payment journey, identifying where issues occurred, and producing clear, accurate responses that meet the bank’s expectations.

• Understand what each banking partner needs to see in a response and tailor your output

accordingly — whether that’s a transaction trail, a merchant explanation, supporting documentation, or a combination.

• Question what you find — don’t close a query at the first plausible answer. If something looks unusual or doesn’t add up, dig further and escalate to the Fraud & Risk Manager where needed.

nothing falls through the cracks and that patterns across queries are surfaced proactively.

Merchant Risk Monitoring

• Carry out day-to-day merchant risk monitoring across the Ryft portfolio — reviewing

transaction activity, volumes, and behavioural patterns to identify anomalies that may indicate fraud, policy breach, or elevated risk.

closely with the Fraud & Risk Manager to ensure monitoring activity informs rule tuning and threshold decisions.

• Flag merchants or sub-merchants exhibiting patterns of concern, documenting your findings clearly and escalating where a risk response is required.

• Support chargeback and dispute monitoring at the merchant level, identifying accounts with elevated dispute rates and feeding that data into the wider fraud analysis process.

• Maintain accurate, audit-ready records of monitoring activity and risk decisions in line with FCA expectations and internal policy.

Cross-functional Collaboration

• Work closely with the Fraud & Risk Manager to ensure partner query intelligence and merchant monitoring findings are connected — a query from an acquirer about a specific merchant should inform, and be informed by, what you’re seeing in monitoring.

• Liaise with the underwriting team where partner queries or merchant monitoring activity raises questions about how a merchant was onboarded or what their risk profile should be.

acquirer, payment facilitator, or bank — with direct exposure to acquirer or banking partner

simultaneously without losing track of timelines or detail.

Working alongside the team, you'll help publish our major data-driven campaigns, own the communications for a couple of our newest products, and support our public affairs and policy work. You'll also help with the BAU media activities that keep iwoca front-of-mind with key journalists and stakeholders.

Examples of the type of work you'll be doing:

1. Support data-driven PR campaigns

Working with the team, you'll run several established data-driven campaigns:

  • Top 25 UK Cities for SME Jobs: Our annual ranking combines ONS employment data, business figures, and economic indicators. You can refine the methodology if needed, analyse the latest data, and craft narratives for regional and national media.

  • SME survey research: Twice a year you'll help commission original survey research, working with established research partners to design questionnaires capturing timely SME sentiment. You'll help ensure we generate "business news" coverage that responds to real economic issues.

  • You'll be comfortable working with raw datasets - not just presenting finished analysis. Spotting surprising findings, identifying regional variations, understanding which angles interest journalists versus policymakers.

2. Start shouting about our new products

You'll eventually own the communications for a couple of iwoca's newest products, working directly with Venture Leads to drive awareness and customer acquisition. Here are a few we've just launched that you could be working on:

  • Credit Compass: Our credit-building tool helping SMEs improve their scores. You'll identify customer success stories, translate credit score trends into compelling narratives, and position this as iwoca's answer to the credit access gap.

  • SME Insurance: Help launch this proposition to market - identifying angles around why SMEs need this product and announce new strategic partners as and when we secure them.

  • iwoca Credit Card: You'll be involved from the ground up - understanding competitive positioning, identifying what's newsworthy in a crowded market, building a launch campaign that breaks through.

  • iwocaPay (launched in 2020): Our instant payment solution - you'll help scale awareness as this product continues to grow, finding ongoing news hooks beyond what we've already done in recent years.

  • For each product, you'll get under the hood with the Venture Leads - understanding commercial objectives, customer pain points, competitive landscape - then translating that into comms plans that drive both coverage and business outcomes. You'll own two products, with the split decided once you're in the job.

3. Support our public affairs and policy work

iwoca works with government and policymakers to make the case for better access to finance for small businesses. You'll support this work, engaging with relevant government departments, industry bodies and ministers where relevant. This could include:

  • Tracking policy and regulatory developments that affect SMEs and SME lending.

  • Helping draft consultation responses, policy briefings and position papers.

  • Using our lending and survey data to build the evidence behind our policy positions.

  • Preparing briefing materials for meetings with officials, industry bodies and ministers.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Up to two years' experience in communications, PR, public affairs, policy, journalism or a related field. Internships and placements count, and we welcome recent graduates.

  • Excellent writing skills with the ability to craft data-driven stories, press releases, briefing materials, and media pitches that cut through.

  • Ability to work at pace across multiple projects simultaneously, with strong organisational skills.

  • You'll need to be confident managing and analysing data with either Excel or Google Sheets.

  • A genuine interest in the economy, policy and politics, and how they affect small businesses.

Bonus:

  • Some experience in, or a strong interest in, tech, fintech, financial services or B2B technology.

  • Experience in public affairs, policy or government relations, or an understanding of how policy is made.

  • Any exposure to product launches or translating complex propositions into accessible narratives.

  • Experience pitching to journalists or securing coverage in relevant press.

  • Comfortable working with senior stakeholders.

  • Commercial awareness and understanding of what drives media coverage in fintech and SME finance.

  • Familiarity with media monitoring tools (e.g., Signal AI, Cision) and ability to analyse coverage data to inform strategy.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

title: Quality Assurance Officer
description:
An exciting opportunity to join Leafio as a Quality Officer and play an important role in shaping the future of our pharmaceutical wholesale operations.

As Leafio continues to grow, we are looking for an experienced and detail-oriented Quality Officer who is passionate about maintaining high standards of quality, compliance and patient safety.

This is an opportunity to be part of a business at a pivotal stage of its journey, helping to establish and develop our quality processes as we build a compliant, efficient and reliable pharmaceutical supply chain.

Working closely with our Responsible Person and wider operational teams, you will play a key role in maintaining our Quality Management System, supporting regulatory compliance and ensuring that the medicines moving through our supply chain meet the highest standards.

We are looking for someone who brings hands-on experience within a regulated pharmaceutical environment, a strong understanding of Good Distribution Practice (GDP) and the confidence to take ownership of quality activities in a fast-paced, evolving business.

If you enjoy working collaboratively, have a keen eye for detail and want to make a meaningful contribution to a growing organisation, this could be a fantastic next step in your career.

What is the job?

We are looking for an experienced Quality Officer to join Leafio at a pivotal stage of our growth. This is a unique opportunity to join an ambitious team as we establish our pharmaceutical wholesale operation and secure the licences required to import, store and distribute medicinal products across the UK.

As part of the Quality team, you will ensure the daily activities are actioned and monitored and meet the highest standards of Good Distribution Practice (GDP), regulatory compliance and product quality.

You will play a critical role in ensuring that all medicinal products received, stored and supplied by Leafio comply with GDP, MHRA requirements (esp Reg 167), internal Quality Management Systems (QMS) standards, and customer expectations.

What will you be doing?

  • Ensure that Deviations, change controls, risk management and CAPAs are actioned according to their target date of completion

  • Raise Deviations, change controls, risk managements and CAPAs when needed and support in the investigations where relevant

  • Maintain and update the QMS (SOPs, policies, forms, logs)

  • Draft standard operating procedures, distribute for reviewing and finalising the procedures

  • Manage document control, versioning, training records and archiving

  • Support preparation of quality management review

  • Deliver GDP and QMS training to the relevant departments where needed

  • Support with batch traceability, Certificate of Analysis (CoA) documentation and batch release confirmations/verifications

  • Support with customers’ complaints and ensure timelines are adhered to

  • Support the Responsible Person (RP) in maintaining compliance and safeguarding product quality throughout the supply chain.

  • Actively collaborating with cross-functional teams (e.g. pharmacy, warehouse)

  • Participating and supporting in audits (internal/external) and inspections where required

  • Any other tasks deemed necessary by the Responsible Person (RP)

What do you need?

  • Knowledge of Good Manufacturing (GMP) or Good Distribution Practice (GDP) and the regulatory framework governing pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution

  • Proven experience working within a GMDP regulated pharmaceutical environment, (ideally supporting wholesale distribution and importation), with more than 2 years experience

  • Proven experience of dealing with a Quality Management Systems (QMS), including but not limited to Complaints, CAPAs, Deviations risk management, change control, self inspections/internal audits

  • Proven experience in dealing with unlicensed products (especially in accordance with Regulation 167)

  • Excellent attention to detail and analytical skills

  • Strong communication and report-writing ability

  • Highly organised, able to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines

Desirable

  • Experience or exposure to Importation of unlicensed products from outside the EEA

  • Experience in working with an ERP system

  • Previous experience working within the medical cannabis sector

  • Previous experience in releasing products (QC-Quality control)

What we offer:

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three + 8 bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Private Healthcare Scheme

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more

  • Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave


About Us

At Leafio, we’re building a smarter, more resilient pharmaceutical supply chain that gives pharmacies fast and reliable access to the medicines they need, when they need them.

By working directly with manufacturers and creating a more efficient wholesale model, we’re improving stock availability, simplifying distribution and helping to make medicines more affordable for patients. Everything we do is focused on creating a supply chain that is responsive, transparent and equipped to better support healthcare providers across the UK.

We are an ambitious, fast-growing business with exciting plans for the future. This is an opportunity to make a genuine impact, help shape how we grow and join a team that is modernising pharmaceutical distribution from the ground up.

title: Clinical Pharmacist
description:
At Montu, we are transforming access to medical cannabis treatment across the UK, and our Clinical Pharmacists play an important role in delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

We are looking for an experienced Clinical Pharmacist (Independent Prescriber) to join our growing London team. What is the job?

As a Clinical Pharmacist (Independent Prescriber), you will provide safe, effective and personalised treatment to patients with a wide range of clinical needs.

Working closely with our multidisciplinary team, you will be responsible for clinically reviewing prescriptions, prescribing appropriate treatments and providing expert clinical guidance to patients and colleagues.

You will also contribute to the development of clinical pathways, support patient and staff education and play an important role in maintaining the highest standards of clinical care.

This is a hybrid position based at our King's Cross office in London, requiring three days on site and two days working remotely.

What will you be doing?

  • Clinically check and review cannabis-based medicinal product (CBPM) prescriptions to ensure safety, accuracy and appropriateness.

  • Prescribe medicines as an Independent Prescriber, tailoring treatment to individual patient needs.

  • Provide expert clinical guidance to patients and prescribers on treatment options.

  • Maintain accurate and comprehensive patient records in accordance with GPhC standards.

  • Support the dispensary team with complex clinical queries and prescribing-related matters.

  • Deliver education and training on CBPM to patients, clinicians and colleagues.

  • Collaborate with the wider Clinical and Pharmacy teams to ensure a safe and effective patient journey.

  • Contribute to the development of clinical pathways and improvements in patient care.

  • Ensure all clinical activities are conducted in accordance with professional, regulatory and organisational standards.

What are we looking for?

  • GPhC registered pharmacist with an Independent Prescriber (IP) qualification.

  • A minimum of two years of prescribing experience.

  • Experience working within a clinical setting.

  • Previous knowledge or experience of cannabis-based medicinal products is desirable but not essential, as specialist training will be provided.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to engage with patients and clinical colleagues.

  • Strong clinical judgement and the ability to make safe, evidence-based prescribing decisions.

  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.

  • A proactive, resourceful and solutions-focused approach.

  • High attention to detail and a commitment to patient safety and clinical governance.

  • A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.

What do we offer?

  • Generous Annual Leave: 25 days holiday, increasing to 27 days after one year and 30 days after three years, plus 8 bank holidays.

  • Private Healthcare Scheme.

  • Hybrid Working: A combination of office-based and remote working.

  • Cycle-to-Work Scheme: Supporting healthier and more sustainable commuting.

  • Career Development: Opportunities to develop specialist clinical knowledge, collaborate across teams and represent Montu at industry events.

  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity Leave.

Why Montu?

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicinal products (CBPM), committed to improving access to treatment for patients across the UK.

We are helping to shape the future of medical cannabis healthcare, bringing together experienced clinicians, pharmacists and healthcare professionals who share a commitment to delivering safe, accessible and personalised care.

Joining Montu means becoming part of a growing organisation where your clinical expertise is valued, your professional development is supported and the work you do has a direct impact on patients' lives

title: Medical Lead
description:
Are you an experienced doctor with a passion for developing others and delivering exceptional patient care?

At Montu, we are looking for a Medical Team Lead to join our growing Clinical team, combining clinical practice with the opportunity to lead, mentor and develop a team of doctors.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys supporting others, has experience providing clinical guidance and supervision, and is confident in building strong working relationships with clinicians and consultants.

You will play a key role in supporting the professional development of our Junior Clinical Fellows (JCFs), helping them build confidence, develop greater clinical autonomy and deliver safe, high-quality patient care.

As we continue to grow, this is an opportunity to bring your clinical expertise and leadership skills into an evolving area of healthcare, helping to shape and support the next generation of clinicians while making a meaningful difference to patients' lives.

What is the job?

As a Medical Team Lead, you will provide day-to-day leadership, support and guidance to a team of clinicians, ensuring they are well-supervised, well-supported, and progressing safely towards greater clinical autonomy. You will act as the primary link between clinicians and consultants, coordinating supervision, escalation pathways, and feedback loops so that patient care stays safe and consistent.

You will combine your own clinical practice with people leadership, taking ownership of fellow development, consultant engagement, governance, and training within your team, while working alongside other Team Leads to keep standards consistent across the wider service.

You will be the first point of contact for JCF’s requiring guidance on professional or personal development and appraisal or revalidation. You will also act as a trusted contact for consultants raising concerns about supervision and workload.

What will you be doing?

Clinician Line Management

  • Act as the named line manager/lead for a cohort of clinicians, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, and pastoral support.

  • Conduct regular 1:1s with each fellow, tracking progress against objectives, competencies, and rotation/training milestones.

  • Identify clinicians who are struggling early, and put support plans in place in collaboration with consultants and HR/medical education leads.

  • Assist with the onboarding and induction experience for new clinicians — inductions, shadowing, buddy systems, and early check-ins.

  • Support the management of day-to-day workforce logistics for the clinicians: rota input, leave requests, sickness/absence, and shift coverage, working with the operations team.

  • Recognise and celebrate good performance, and manage underperformance or conduct concerns through appropriate, documented processes alongside our HR team.

Consultant Engagement

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with consultants.

  • Act as the escalation point for consultants — surfacing concerns about supervision quality, caseload, or clinical support gaps.

  • Coordinate consultant and JCF annual appraisals or revalidation.

  • Gather and act on consultant feedback regarding clinical safety and any recurring themes.

  • Support scheduling and coverage conversations with consultants (clinics, on-call, teaching sessions).

Clinical & Patient Support

  • Act as a point of escalation for complex clinical cases and patient concerns.

  • Support clinicians through complaints, incidents, and governance issues involving their clinical decisions.

  • Provide direct clinical mentoring, and know when to route a case to a consultant.

  • Promote safe prescribing and adherence to clinical standards appropriate to clinicians’ training level.

Governance, Quality & Audit

  • Support compliance with clinical policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements across the fellow cohort.

  • Support clinical audits and quality improvement projects, involving clinicians in QI work as a development opportunity.

  • Analyse audit and incident themes specific to JCFs (e.g. common escalation triggers, training gaps) and use these to shape training priorities.

  • Work with governance and operational teams on regulatory readiness.

Operational Excellence & Change

  • Monitor clinician workload, rota adherence, professionalism and service coverage; flag risks early.

  • Contribute to process improvements that affect how fellows are supervised, escalate, or are trained.

  • Track and report on team performance metrics: fellow progression, incident trends, audit outcomes, consultant feedback themes.

  • Collaborate with other Team Leads to keep clinician management and consultant engagement approaches consistent across services.

Training & Education

  • Support the induction programmes for incoming clinicians from a medical perspective.

  • Identify individual and cohort-wide development needs, working with consultants and training and education teams to close gaps.

  • Involvement in the organisation and/or deliver teaching sessions and case reviews.

  • Champion a culture of learning, feedback, and continuous improvement across the fellow-consultant relationship.

This list is not exhaustive. As the business evolves, responsibilities may change and develop over time.

What do you need?

  • GMC registration with an active licence to practise and good professional standing.

  • Experience supervising, managing, or mentoring junior doctors/clinical fellows is desirable.

  • Experience working alongside or liaising with consultants in a clinical or operational capacity is desirable.

  • Understanding of clinical governance, incident management, complaints handling, audit, and quality improvement.

  • Confidence managing sensitive people-management conversations (performance, wellbeing, escalations).

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence both junior and senior clinicians.

  • Experience working within digital healthcare, telemedicine, private healthcare, or fast-paced healthcare environments is desirable.

  • Comfortable using clinical systems, rostering tools, and healthcare technology platforms.

  • Adaptable, proactive, and solutions-focused, with a genuine interest in developing junior talent.

What we offer:

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three + 8 bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Private Healthcare Scheme

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more

  • Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave

About Us

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey.

As a fast-growing organisation, we offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers while contributing to meaningful change in healthcare. At Montu UK, your work has a direct impact on improving patients’ lives and expanding access to modern medical treatments.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist PAYE
description:
An opportunity to help patients who have run out of options

 

For many people living with chronic pain, the journey has been long. They have tried multiple medications, procedures and therapies, yet their pain continues to impact every aspect of daily life. By the time they reach us, many are looking for another option where conventional treatment has fallen short.

We are Montu UK, one of the UK's largest medical cannabis clinics, and we are looking for Consultants specialising in Pain Management to join our clinical team.

 

About the role

You will assess and manage patients exploring cannabis based medicines, making the clinical decision on whether treatment is appropriate and managing their care from there. This is an evolving area of medicine where the evidence base continues to grow, giving you the opportunity to help shape how cannabis based medicines are used within pain management in the UK.

You do not need previous experience with cannabis based medicines. We are looking for experienced Pain Management Consultants with sound clinical judgement, an open mind and a genuine interest in improving outcomes for patients with complex chronic pain. We provide comprehensive specialist training, and our multidisciplinary model means you are never working in isolation. Nurses and pharmacists complete pre consultation and follow up prescribing tasks, allowing you to focus on clinical decision making and patient care.

 

What you will be doing:

  • Provide high quality care for patients seeking medical cannabis treatment.

  • Conduct patient consultations, including assessment and ongoing management.

  • Engage in clinical outcome data collection to support evidence based practices.

  • Contribute to clinical governance and maintain robust patient care standards.

  • Collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team, including nurses and pharmacists.

  • Participate in ongoing training and professional development, including bespoke specialist training in cannabis based medicines (CBMPs).

     

What you need:

  • Full GMC Registration

  • Completion of Specialist Training (CCST/CCT) or equivalent certification

  • On the GMC Specialist Register for Pain

  • Demonstrated interest in alternative therapies

  • Willingness to participate in data collection and reporting

     

Why join us?

  • Highly Competitive Salary: £190,000 - £275,000 FTE, pro rata for part time roles based on experience and hours worked.

  • Flexible Working: Full time or part time options available

  • Comprehensive Indemnity Coverage: Montu will cover all professional and clinical indemnity insurance for your work with us

  • Private Healthcare

  • Work-Life Balance: No night shifts or on call requirements

  • Cutting Edge Training: Access to CPD accredited medical cannabis education and specialist in house training from industry leaders

  • Collaborative Environment: Join a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals

  • Personal Growth: Be part of a pioneering field and shape the future of medical cannabis care in the UK

Training & Development:

  • Attendance at a recognised Medical Cannabis Course for Specialist Physicians (sponsored by Montu)

  • Specialist training delivered by experts, including Prof Anup Mathew (Consultant Psychiatrist) and Dr Gerard Sinovich (Pain Management Consultant).

  • Ongoing support and training on clinical protocols, prescribing practices, and Montu’s system usage

Working arrangements:

  • Remote Role: Flexible working hours and days

  • Session Structure:

  • Standard session length: 4 hours

  • Appointment duration: 15 minutes (new and existing patients)

Montu’s multidisciplinary model allows consultants to focus on prescribing and patient care, while nurses and pharmacists handle pre consultation and follow up tasks.

If you are passionate about innovative patient care, thrive in a dynamic environment, and are looking to make a real impact in the field of medical cannabis, we would love to hear from you!

Sessions:

Each standard session consists of 4 hours of patient consultations. Clinicians can choose their preferred working days and hours, with sessions spread flexibly if needed.

To support onboarding, clinicians are required to commit to a minimum of 2 sessions per week/ 8 hours initially, to ensure they become proficient with Montu’s platform.

Appointment Durations:

Appointments are 15 minutes in length for new and existing patients as Montu operates a multidisciplinary approach, leveraging a clinical skills mix where nurses and pharmacists handle pre-consultation and follow-up prescribing tasks allowing Consultants to focus on prescribing and patient care.

 

About MONTU

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis based medicines (CBPM). We are committed to transforming lives by improving access to safe, effective treatments and offering an exceptional standard of care. Our dynamic and supportive work environment is the perfect place for you to grow professionally while making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.
